page: OVHcloud h100-760 is a GPU-accelerated server designed for intensive computational workloads. It features 60 dedicated physical cores powered by AMD EPYC 9354 processors running at 3.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 760.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.67 GB per core. For acceleration, the server is equipped with two NVIDIA H100 GPUs from the Hopper architecture, delivering a combined 160 GB of HBM3 VRAM. Local storage consists of 4040 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and network connectivity is supported by a 16 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

In benchmark evaluations, the server exhibits top-tier performance in several key areas. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as PassMark CPU and physics tests. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks ranks in the top 10%, though large-block uncached read and write operations fall into the middle 50% range. For specialized workloads, the dual H100 GPUs deliver top-tier performance in large language model inference, achieving top 10% speeds for prompt processing and text generation across 7B and 70B parameter models.

From a resource-density perspective, the h100-760 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring massive parallel processing and local storage, combining high-capacity NVMe storage with dedicated GPU accelerators. However, a potential tradeoff is the average performance in large-block memory bandwidth and standard multi-core Geekbench tasks, indicating that the system is highly optimized for GPU-bound and vector-heavy operations rather than general-purpose memory-bound tasks. This server is suited for large language model inference, deep learning training, ray tracing, and complex scientific simulations.
